A1.justification: Both complete 17-page PDFs describe GaussRender and include readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and six supplementary pages. Content can be reliably matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original GaussRender training and evaluation results on three occupancy benchmarks, along with camera, loss, and hyperparameter ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original benchmark results and reports additional rendering-only comparisons, camera ablations, and KITTI-360 analyses.

M1.justification: v3 introduces an experimental Dynamic camera-selection variant: elevated cameras positioned along a ring target the voxel with highest 3D cross-entropy (Appendix E.4). This changes the procedure for that tested variant; the principal Gaussianization pipeline, opacity prediction, and losses in Equations 1–6 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use SurroundOcc-nuScenes, Occ3D-nuScenes, and SSCBench-KITTI360 for driving-scene semantic occupancy prediction. Added supervision variants and visibility-specific measurements concern retained data and tasks, rather than new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 2 substantially expands the reported rendering-method comparison with SelfOcc, OccNerf, GaussianOcc, and static/temporal RenderOcc against fully trained rendering-only GaussRender. v2 already reports RenderOcc elsewhere but lacks this comparison and the three self-supervised comparators. The main benchmark and RayIoU comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The camera study changes from 2D-only training on two datasets with IoU/mIoU reporting to 2D-only versus joint 2D+3D training on Occ3D with mIoU reporting; the 20% subsets remain. New protocols include the fully trained rendering-only comparison and KITTI-360 evaluation using visible-voxel, sensor-image, and depth-L1 metrics. These do not establish changes to the retained benchmark experiments.

E4.justification: The principal camera ablation is substantially redesigned to test interaction with supervision type, adding Dynamic positioning while removing Stereo and the SurroundOcc camera-study results. v3 also adds a KITTI-360 breakdown examining whether gains concentrate in visible geometry and rendered observations. Existing loss-component, Gaussian-scale, loss-weight, and camera-count ablations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v3's new attribution of per-class variation to learning variance is an interpretation, without accompanying statistical estimation or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds 25.3 mIoU for fully trained rendering-only GaussRender and new KITTI-360 results, including depth L1 of 1.394 without versus 1.173 with GaussRender. Camera results are replaced and expanded: Occ3D Random scores 12.0 in v2, whereas Fully Random scores 6.9 in v3; incompletely specified sampling prevents treating this as a verified same-setting decline. Main benchmark, RayIoU, BeV, and per-class scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The occupancy formulation, Gaussian projection and compositing equations, loss definitions, and Gaussian-scale reasoning are retained. Neither version adds or revises a theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The introduction and contribution list narrow claims from state-of-the-art performance across settings and benchmarks to consistent improvements across models. The claim of loosely sensitive hyperparameters is removed. Core projective-consistency, compatibility, and efficiency contributions remain; the abstract and conclusion still claim state-of-the-art results.

C2.justification: Section 4.4.1 now explains preferred viewpoints through 2D-only versus joint supervision, replacing the earlier emphasis on visible versus occluded reconstruction. New passages attribute Dynamic failures to unstable supervision and KITTI gains to removing visibility artifacts. Appendix F additionally attributes class-level variations to learning variance without statistical support.

D1.justification: Appendix E.4 documents the new error-directed camera variant but omits v2's explicit 2-meter elevation, 20-degree downward tilt, and ±10-degree random perturbations. The RayIoU table also loses most frame-count disclosures. Optimizer settings, hardware, training budgets, computational-cost information, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference list and related-work discussion remain substantively unchanged. New Table 2 and Section 4.2 extend positioning against supervised and self-supervised rendering methods through supervision source, image-label density, memory overhead, and temporal inputs, including a new rendering-only state-of-the-art claim.

P1.justification: There are localized abstract and introduction edits, rewritten camera-study explanations, and revised terminology emphasizing visual consistency. BeV analysis moves from Section 4.3 to Appendix D, and camera-strategy descriptions move to Appendix E.4. The overall narrative and main section structure remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v3 adds two comparison tables, redesigns the camera table with viewpoint illustrations, relocates the BeV table to the appendix, and removes the RayIoU Frames column. Appendix plots are repositioned with small axis and legend adjustments. The principal schematics, qualitative panels, and overall two-column layout remain.

improvement.justification: The joint-supervision camera ablation tests viewpoint selection under the paper's principal training objective, and the new KITTI-360 visibility/image/depth breakdown better supports its artifact-reduction argument. These provide a limited overall gain while established benchmark results remain stable. Benefits are tempered by removing the SurroundOcc camera analysis, exact camera parameters, and most RayIoU frame counts; the new rendering-method comparison also uses differing supervision sources.
